notes: 1. GHNG- = buyer registration/record prefix used throughout this module (e.g. GHNG-2000000009). REQ-NNNNN = the callback Request ID shown in the table's first data column (e.g. REQ-00075).

2. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] = a disposable UAT record/state must be supplied before executing this test (e.g. a PENDING callback request you are allowed to act on, a buyer registered for the Create flow, an isAvailable=false SM, a second SM login for scoping tests, API bearer token, or DB read access). NEVER invent these values.
3. [VERIFY WITH DEV] = behaviour not confirmed in BRD/FRD/FS/Workflow; confirm before treating Pass/Fail as authoritative.

4. No live-portal mutations are assumed safe. Any action that WRITES to a callback request (submit a VC Outcome / create a callback request / bulk-assign / reassign) is stateful on UAT and requires explicit user authorisation before execution — those TCs carry [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED]. Capture-only operations (open a drawer, open a modal, open a dropdown, type a search, Cancel out) are safe and need no authorisation.

5. KPI / summary cards at the top of the page show global totals for the logged-in SM's scope and do NOT recompute when the table is searched, sorted, or column-filtered. [VERIFY WITH DEV] whether clicking a KPI card filters the table (SM_CB_020) — not documented.
6. Auth is Mobile-OTP only (no password). SM master OTP = 258369; UAT SM mobile = 8888888888. Successful login lands directly on /sales-manager/callback-requests (the default SM workspace).

7. SCOPING RULE (FS 1.2 / BRD-SM 4): a standard Sales Manager (role 5) sees ONLY their own assigned requests; a Sales Manager Admin (role 4) sees ALL requests system-wide and has the 'Select Sales Manager' filter + bulk Assign action. Tests that require BOTH roles need a second login and are marked [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED].

8. VC OUTCOME GLOSSARY — the 'Capture VC Outcome' modal exposes exactly 10 codes (visual-memory + FS 4.3): VC Done with Preference (VC_DONE_PREFERENCE), VC Done No Preference (VC_DONE_NO_PREFERENCE), Future Scheduled (FUTURE_SCHEDULED), Future Rescheduled (FUTURE_RESCHEDULED), Missed Scheduled NC (MISSED_SCHEDULED_NC), Not Interested Lost (NOT_INTERESTED_LOST), Never Connected (NEVER_CONNECTED), TL Lost (TL_LOST), VC 2-Done (VC_2_DONE), CP to Drive Preference (CP_TO_DRIVE_PREFERENCE). Only VC_DONE_PREFERENCE and VC_2_DONE trigger the VC_REQUEST discount offer (WF 4 / BRD-SM 4.4).

9. STATUS VALUES (FS 1.5): REQUESTED -> SCHEDULED -> CONFIRMED -> COMPLETED, with RESCHEDULED branching from SCHEDULED. In the live UI the row Status badge surfaces as PENDING (ant-tag-yellow) and MEETING DONE / CONFIRMED (ant-tag-green); the status-column filter dropdown lists Pending, Resent Invite, Sent Invite, Meeting Done. COMPLETED is effectively UNREACHABLE in the current backend (service catches ENUM truncation and falls back to CONFIRMED — FS 1.5 note / BUG-SM-002).

10. DOC_DRIFT-CBR-001 — The FS/BRD/Workflow describe THREE separate UI surfaces: 'Schedule Meeting' (ScheduleMeetingModal, FS Feature 2), 'Confirm Meeting' (ConfirmMeetingModal, FS Feature 3) and 'Record Outcome' (FeedbackDrawer, FS Feature 4). The LIVE UI (visual-memory 2026-06-05) has NONE of these as separate surfaces — the row 'more' (3-dot) menu has a SINGLE item 'Capture VC Outcome' that opens one modal (Registration No, Customer Name, Select Outcome dropdown, Cancel, Submit), and that modal drives the status transition. Docs are stale; tests are grounded in the live single-modal UI. BA Agent to update FS Features 2/3/4 to describe the unified Capture VC Outcome modal in the next doc-sync.

11. DOC_DRIFT-CBR-002 — Assignment: BRD-SM 4.1 and FS 1.7 / WF item-4 both still describe 'round-robin by lastRequestAssignedAt'. The actual implementation is LEAST-LOADED (SM with fewest active requests); round-robin code is disabled (callback-request-sm.service.js:338-349) and when an SM Admin creates a request managerId = their own id (no auto-distribute). Tests assert least-loaded / self-assign per the FSD-CORRECTION; the prose round-robin claims in the docs are stale.

12. DOC_DRIFT-CBR-003 — Create Callback Request fields. FS 5.3 lists fields Customer / Preferred Date / Preferred Time / Notes. The LIVE Create drawer (visual-memory) is a two-step flow: (1) buyer Search -> results table with radio select; (2) form with To (Buyer Email) [readonly auto-filled], To (Sales Manager Email) [readonly auto-filled], CC (multi-tag), Select Date & Time (single Ant DatePicker — not separate Date + Time), and a Create button gated by disabled-state (no inline error messages, no Notes field visible). Tests follow the live drawer.

13. DOC_DRIFT-CBR-004 — Create assignment. FS 5.4 says 'Round-robin assignment applies — may be assigned to any available SM'. Per DOC_DRIFT-CBR-002 this is least-loaded, and for an SM Admin creator managerId = self. Asserted accordingly.

14. SECURITY / INTEGRATION scope: LeadSquared (LSQ) is EXCLUDED from execution — VC-outcome / activity sync to LSQ is asserted only as a documented downstream expectation, never by calling LSQ. Microsoft Teams link generation, Kaleyra (WhatsApp/click-to-call/SMS) and the buyer feedback token URL are external side-effects — assert the portal-visible artefact (e.g. Meeting Link column populated) and mark the dispatch itself [VERIFY WITH DEV] / out-of-scope where it leaves the portal.

15. ID SCHEME: both historical prefixes are preserved — SM_CB_NNN / SM_CB_FSD_NNN (baseline) and TC_CBR_<TYPE>_NNN (supplemental, single shared running counter). New supplemental TCs continue the TC_CBR counter from 056. No existing ID is renumbered.

tcs.precond: The SM is on the Callback Requests page with at least one row.
tcs.steps:
1. Click the green eye icon in a row's Actions cell.
2. Observe the drawer.
tcs.expected: A right-side drawer titled 'Callback Request Details' opens with three tabs: Callback Request, Feedback, Callback History (visual-memory details-drawer).

tcs.scenario: To verify the Callback Request tab is read-only for a PENDING row
tcs.description: Verify that the default Callback Request tab shows read-only customer info for a PENDING row with no editable fields.
tcs.precond: A PENDING row exists.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the details drawer for a PENDING row (e.g. REQ-00075).
2. Read the Callback Request tab content.
tcs.expected: The tab shows Customer Information, Registration Preferences, Description and a Customer Units table as read-only — no editable inputs, only a close button (visual-memory callback-details-drawer-pending.png).

tcs.scenario: To verify the Callback Request tab on a MEETING DONE row shows CONFIRMED
tcs.description: Verify that the details drawer for a MEETING DONE row shows the same sections with Status = CONFIRMED.
tcs.precond: A MEETING DONE row exists (e.g. REQ-00073).
tcs.steps:
1. Open the details drawer for a MEETING DONE row.
2. Read the Status shown.
tcs.expected: The same read-only sections are shown and the Status is CONFIRMED (visual-memory callback-details-drawer-meetingdone.png).

tcs.scenario: To verify the Feedback tab shows all SM Feedback fields
tcs.description: Verify that the Feedback tab shows the Sales Manager Feedback section with all documented fields plus the Registration Preferences sub-section.
tcs.precond: A MEETING DONE row with SM feedback submitted exists.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the details drawer for a MEETING DONE row.
2. Click the Feedback tab.
3. Read the fields.
tcs.expected: The Feedback tab shows Sales Manager Feedback fields (Submitted at, Intent, Allocation Day Confirmation, Typology, Budget, Floor Preference Min-Max, Lost Reason, Home Loan, Parking Required, Remark, Next Step) and a Registration Preferences sub-section listing TOWER/UNIT picks (e.g. Tower 8 - Crest unit 1301) (visual-memory callback-details-feedback-tab.png).

tcs.scenario: To verify the Callback History tab shows the history table
tcs.description: Verify that the Callback History tab shows a per-registration history table with the documented columns.
tcs.precond: A row with prior callback history exists.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the details drawer.
2. Click the Callback History tab.
3. Read the table columns.
tcs.expected: The tab shows 'Callback History for GHNG-...' with columns Request ID, Requested At, Manager Name, VC Outcome, Status, View (visual-memory callback-details-history-tab.png). This reflects the previousMeetings history (WF rule 7).

tcs.scenario: To verify the details drawer close button dismisses the drawer
tcs.description: Verify that the drawer's close control dismisses the details drawer and returns to the table.
tcs.precond: The details drawer is open.
tcs.steps: 1. Click the drawer's close (X) control.
tcs.expected: The drawer closes and the underlying table is shown unchanged.

tcs.scenario: To verify the eye icon exposes no SM action surface
tcs.description: Verify that the details drawer is purely read-only and exposes no Schedule/Confirm/Record action buttons (those live only in the more-menu modal).
tcs.precond: The details drawer is open for any row.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the details drawer.
2. Scan all three tabs for any action button.
tcs.expected: No Schedule Meeting / Confirm Meeting / Record Outcome / Submit button appears in the drawer — it is read-only (visual-memory). Per DOC_DRIFT-CBR-001 the only write surface is the Capture VC Outcome modal from the more menu.

subModules.name: More Menu — Capture VC Outcome (open / display)

tcs.scenario: To verify the more menu shows a single Capture VC Outcome item on a PENDING row
tcs.description: Verify that clicking the 3-dot more icon on a PENDING row opens a dropdown whose only item is 'Capture VC Outcome'.
tcs.precond: A PENDING row exists.
tcs.steps:
1. Click the 3-dot more icon on a PENDING row.
2. Read the dropdown items.
tcs.expected: The dropdown shows exactly one item: 'Capture VC Outcome' (visual-memory callback-row-more-menu.png).

tcs.scenario: To verify the more menu shows the same single item on a MEETING DONE row
tcs.description: Verify that the more menu on a MEETING DONE row also shows only 'Capture VC Outcome' (no extra status-specific actions).
tcs.precond: A MEETING DONE row exists.
tcs.steps:
1. Click the 3-dot more icon on a MEETING DONE row.
2. Read the dropdown items.
tcs.expected: The dropdown shows the single item 'Capture VC Outcome' — the menu is identical across statuses (visual-memory callback-row-more-menu-meetingdone.png).

tcs.scenario: To verify Capture VC Outcome opens the modal with the PENDING row context
tcs.description: Verify that selecting 'Capture VC Outcome' on a PENDING row opens the modal pre-filled with that row's Registration No and Customer Name.
tcs.precond: A PENDING row exists.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the more menu on a PENDING row (e.g. REQ-00075).
2. Click 'Capture VC Outcome'.
3. Read the modal header.
tcs.expected: The 'Capture VC Outcome' modal opens showing Registration No and Customer Name from the row, a 'Select Outcome' dropdown (placeholder 'Please select an outcome'), and Cancel + Submit buttons with Submit disabled (visual-memory callback-capture-vc-outcome-pending.png).

tcs.scenario: To verify Capture VC Outcome can be re-opened on a MEETING DONE row
tcs.description: Verify that the Capture VC Outcome modal can be opened on a MEETING DONE row to re-capture the outcome.
tcs.precond: A MEETING DONE row exists (e.g. REQ-00073, GHNG-2000000009).
tcs.steps:
1. Open the more menu on a MEETING DONE row.
2. Click 'Capture VC Outcome'.
3. Read the modal.
tcs.expected: The same modal opens with that row's Registration No and Customer Name, allowing re-capture of the outcome (visual-memory callback-capture-vc-outcome-meetingdone.png).

tcs.scenario: To verify the outcome dropdown exposes exactly 10 codes
tcs.description: Verify that the 'Select Outcome' dropdown lists exactly the 10 documented vcOutcome codes.
tcs.precond: The Capture VC Outcome modal is open.
tcs.steps:
1. Click the 'Select Outcome' dropdown.
2. Read all options.
tcs.expected: The dropdown shows exactly 10 options: VC Done with Preference, VC Done No Preference, Future Scheduled, Future Rescheduled, Missed Scheduled NC, Not Interested Lost, Never Connected, TL Lost, VC 2-Done, CP to Drive Preference (visual-memory callback-vc-outcome-dropdown.png; matches FS 4.3).

tcs.scenario: To verify the modal header matches the row that opened it
tcs.description: Verify that the Registration No and Customer Name in the modal header exactly match the row from which the modal was opened.
tcs.precond: Two distinct rows exist.
tcs.steps:
1. Open Capture VC Outcome from row A; note the header.
2. Cancel.
3. Open Capture VC Outcome from row B; note the header.
tcs.expected: Each modal's header Registration No + Customer Name match the originating row exactly (no carry-over from the previous open).

tcs.scenario: To verify Submit is disabled while no outcome is selected
tcs.description: Verify that the modal's Submit button is disabled until an outcome is chosen (vcOutcome is required — FS 4.4).
tcs.precond: The Capture VC Outcome modal is open with no outcome selected.
tcs.steps: 1. Observe the Submit button before selecting an outcome.
tcs.expected: Submit is disabled; no inline error message is shown — the form gates submission via the disabled state (visual-memory callback-capture-vc-outcome-validation.png).

tcs.scenario: To verify selecting an outcome enables Submit
tcs.description: Verify that choosing any outcome from the dropdown enables the Submit button.
tcs.precond: The Capture VC Outcome modal is open.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the Select Outcome dropdown.
2. Choose any outcome (e.g. 'VC Done No Preference').
3. Observe the Submit button.
tcs.expected: Submit becomes enabled once an outcome is selected.

tcs.scenario: To verify Submit cannot be forced while the outcome is empty
tcs.description: Verify that the disabled Submit cannot be triggered while no outcome is selected, so no empty submission reaches the backend.
tcs.precond: The Capture VC Outcome modal is open with no outcome selected.
tcs.steps: 1. With no outcome selected, attempt to click Submit.
tcs.expected: Nothing happens; no request is submitted and the modal stays open (Submit remains disabled). [VERIFY WITH DEV] backend also rejects an empty vcOutcome if posted directly (UI-vs-backend split).

tcs.scenario: To verify Cancel closes the modal without submitting
tcs.description: Verify that the Cancel button closes the Capture VC Outcome modal without recording an outcome.
tcs.precond: The Capture VC Outcome modal is open (optionally with an outcome selected).
tcs.steps:
1. Select an outcome (optional).
2. Click Cancel.
tcs.expected: The modal closes, no outcome is recorded, and the row Status / VC Outcome are unchanged.

tcs.scenario: To verify an SM can record an outcome on their own request
tcs.description: Verify that a standard SM can submit a VC Outcome on a request assigned to them. WRITE action — needs authorisation.
tcs.precond: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a disposable callback request assigned to this SM, safe to write to. Requires user authorisation before execution (live mutation).
tcs.steps:
1. Open the more menu on the SM's own disposable request.
2. Click 'Capture VC Outcome'.
3. Select an outcome.
4. Click Submit.
tcs.expected: The outcome is recorded, the row's VC Outcome / SM Feedback updates, and isSmFeedbackSubmitted is set. The system sends the buyer a feedback token URL (SM_CB_109). [VERIFY WITH DEV] exact on-submit confirmation message.

tcs.scenario: To verify VC Done with Preference triggers the VC_REQUEST offer
tcs.description: Verify that submitting outcome 'VC Done with Preference' triggers the VC_REQUEST discount offer for the buyer. WRITE action — needs authorisation.
tcs.precond: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a disposable request safe to write to + offer-visibility check. Requires authorisation (live mutation).
tcs.steps:
1. Open Capture VC Outcome on a disposable request.
2. Select 'VC Done with Preference'.
3. Click Submit.
4. Check the buyer's offers for VC_REQUEST.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] disposable request; outcome VC Done with Preference
tcs.expected: A VC_REQUEST discount offer is created for the buyer's unit purchase (WF item 12 / BRD-SM 4.4). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm where the offer surfaces (RegistrationUnitOffer).

tcs.scenario: To verify VC 2-Done triggers the VC_REQUEST offer
tcs.description: Verify that submitting outcome 'VC 2-Done' also triggers the VC_REQUEST discount offer. WRITE action — needs authorisation.
tcs.precond: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a disposable request safe to write to. Requires authorisation (live mutation).
tcs.steps:
1. Open Capture VC Outcome on a disposable request.
2. Select 'VC 2-Done'.
3. Click Submit.
4. Check the buyer's offers.
tcs.expected: A VC_REQUEST offer is created for the buyer (WF VC Outcome table — VC_2_DONE triggers Yes).

tcs.scenario: To verify other outcomes do NOT trigger the VC_REQUEST offer
tcs.description: Verify that outcomes other than VC_DONE_PREFERENCE / VC_2_DONE do not create a VC_REQUEST offer. WRITE action — needs authorisation.
tcs.precond: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a disposable request safe to write to. Requires authorisation (live mutation).
tcs.steps:
1. Open Capture VC Outcome on a disposable request.
2. Select e.g. 'VC Done No Preference' (or 'Never Connected').
3. Click Submit.
4. Check the buyer's offers.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] disposable request; outcome VC Done No Preference
tcs.expected: No VC_REQUEST offer is created (WF rule 5 — only VC_DONE_PREFERENCE and VC_2_DONE trigger it).

tcs.scenario: To verify a buyer feedback token URL is sent on SM feedback submission
tcs.description: Verify that submitting the SM feedback / VC outcome triggers dispatch of a unique buyer feedback token URL via SMS/WhatsApp. WRITE action — needs authorisation.
tcs.precond: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a disposable request + message-log visibility. Requires authorisation (live mutation).
tcs.steps:
1. Submit a VC outcome on a disposable request.
2. Check the outbound message log / buyer-side for a feedback link.
tcs.expected: A unique token-based feedback URL (buyerFeedbackToken) is generated and sent to the buyer via SMS/WhatsApp (FS 4.4 #4 / WF item 14). [VERIFY WITH DEV] dispatch is via Kaleyra; the actual send is external — confirm the portal records the dispatch.

tcs.scenario: To verify COMPLETED status is not reachable via the UI
tcs.description: Verify the documented gap that a request cannot reach COMPLETED through the normal SM flow — it falls back to CONFIRMED.
tcs.precond: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a disposable request to drive through outcome submission. Requires authorisation (live mutation).
tcs.steps:
1. Submit a VC outcome on a disposable request.
2. Observe the resulting Status.
tcs.expected: The row reaches CONFIRMED, not COMPLETED — the backend catches ENUM truncation and falls back to CONFIRMED (FS 1.5 / BUG-SM-002 / SM_CB_FSD_136). Document the gap; do NOT write a COMPLETED-reached pass case.

tcs.scenario: To verify COMPLETED is unreachable and falls back to CONFIRMED [BUG-REF: BUG-SM-002]
tcs.description: Verify the documented defect that the COMPLETED transition silently falls back to CONFIRMED, so the buyer-feedback completion path never reaches COMPLETED.
tcs.precond: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a disposable request driven to the point of completion + DB read. Requires authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Drive a disposable request through SM outcome submission and buyer feedback.
2. Query the request status in the backend.
tcs.expected: The status persists as CONFIRMED, never COMPLETED (callback-request-sm.service.js:78-87 catches ENUM truncation). Documented as BUG-SM-002 / DOC_DRIFT-CBR-001.

subModules.name: Schedule / Confirm flows (doc-drift — captured as no-separate-surface)

tcs.scenario: To verify there is no separate Schedule Meeting surface in the live UI
tcs.description: Verify the DOC_DRIFT that the FS-documented 'Schedule Meeting' modal (Feature 2) does not exist as a separate UI surface in the live build.
tcs.precond: The SM is on the Callback Requests page; a PENDING (REQUESTED) row exists.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the details drawer and the more menu on a PENDING row.
2. Look for any 'Schedule Meeting' button / date-time + Generate Teams Link + CC form.
tcs.expected: No standalone 'Schedule Meeting' modal exists; the only write surface is the more-menu 'Capture VC Outcome' modal (DOC_DRIFT-CBR-001). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm scheduling/Teams-link generation is folded into outcome capture or the Create flow.

tcs.scenario: To verify there is no separate Confirm Meeting surface in the live UI
tcs.description: Verify the DOC_DRIFT that the FS-documented 'Confirm Meeting' modal (Feature 3) does not exist as a separate UI surface.
tcs.precond: The SM is on the Callback Requests page; a SCHEDULED/MEETING DONE row exists.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the details drawer and more menu on a MEETING DONE row.
2. Look for any 'Confirm Meeting' button.
tcs.expected: No standalone 'Confirm Meeting' control exists (DOC_DRIFT-CBR-001). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm how the CONFIRMED status is reached in the live build.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Meeting Link column shows a clickable Teams link when present
tcs.description: Verify that for a request with a generated Teams meeting link the Meeting column shows a clickable link.
tcs.precond: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a request that has a generated Teams meeting link.
tcs.steps:
1. Find a row with a meeting link.
2. Observe the Meeting column cell.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a row with a Teams link
tcs.expected: The Meeting column shows a clickable Microsoft Teams link (FS 2.5 / BRD-SM Teams Integration). [VERIFY WITH DEV] when/where the link is generated given there is no separate Schedule Meeting modal (DOC_DRIFT-CBR-001).

tcs.scenario: To verify the Create Callback Request button opens the create drawer
tcs.description: Verify that the top-right 'Create Callback Request' button opens the create drawer.
tcs.precond: The SM is on the Callback Requests page.
tcs.steps:
1. Click 'Create Callback Request'.
2. Observe the drawer.
tcs.expected: A right-side drawer titled 'Create Callback Request' opens showing a buyer search input; the email/CC/date fields are present but disabled until a buyer is selected (visual-memory callback-create-drawer.png).

tcs.scenario: To verify buyer search returns a results table with radio selection
tcs.description: Verify that typing a buyer term and clicking Search returns a results table with per-row radio selection and pagination.
tcs.precond: The Create drawer is open. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a buyer search term that returns results (e.g. 'Anjali').
tcs.steps:
1. Type a buyer term in the search input.
2. Click Search.
3. Observe the results.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a buyer term that returns results
tcs.expected: A results table appears (columns Registration Number, Name, Previous Callbacks, Email, Phone) with a radio per row and pagination (e.g. '1-10 of 55 items') (visual-memory callback-create-drawer-searched.png).

tcs.scenario: To verify selecting a buyer auto-populates email fields read-only
tcs.description: Verify that selecting a buyer radio auto-fills the Buyer Email and Sales Manager Email fields as read-only.
tcs.precond: Buyer search results are shown.
tcs.steps:
1. Select a buyer radio.
2. Observe the To (Buyer Email) and To (Sales Manager Email) fields.
tcs.expected: Buyer Email and Sales Manager Email auto-populate and remain read-only; the Create button is still disabled until a date is picked (visual-memory callback-create-buyer-selected.png).

tcs.scenario: To verify the CC field is a multi-tag input
tcs.description: Verify that the CC field accepts multiple email addresses as tags.
tcs.precond: A buyer is selected in the Create drawer.
tcs.steps:
1. Click the CC field (placeholder 'Add CC emails').
2. Type an email and press Enter.
3. Type a second email and press Enter.
tcs.expected: Each entered email becomes a removable tag in the CC multi-select (visual-memory Create drawer form fields).

tcs.scenario: To verify CC accepts only valid email format
tcs.description: Verify whether the CC field validates email format when adding a tag.
tcs.precond: A buyer is selected in the Create drawer.
tcs.steps:
1. Type an invalid value (e.g. 'notanemail') in the CC field.
2. Press Enter.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] CC email-format validation is not documented. Confirm whether an invalid CC entry is rejected or accepted as a tag.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Create button stays disabled until a date is picked
tcs.description: Verify that with a buyer selected but no Date & Time chosen, the Create button remains disabled.
tcs.precond: A buyer is selected; the Select Date & Time field is empty.
tcs.steps:
1. Leave Select Date & Time empty.
2. Observe the Create button.
tcs.expected: Create stays disabled; no inline per-field error is shown — submission is gated by the disabled state (visual-memory callback-create-drawer-validation.png).

tcs.scenario: To verify picking a date enables the Create button
tcs.description: Verify that selecting a Date & Time (with a buyer selected) enables the Create button.
tcs.precond: A buyer is selected.
tcs.steps:
1. Click the Select Date & Time field.
2. Pick a date and time.
3. Observe the Create button.
tcs.testData: Date & Time: a valid future slot
tcs.expected: Create becomes enabled once a buyer is selected and a Date & Time is picked.

tcs.scenario: To verify Create cannot be forced while the date is empty
tcs.description: Verify that the disabled Create cannot be triggered while the date is empty, preventing an incomplete submission.
tcs.precond: A buyer is selected; date empty.
tcs.steps: 1. With the date empty, attempt to click Create.
tcs.expected: Nothing happens; no request is created and the drawer stays open (Create remains disabled).

tcs.scenario: To verify the Create form fields are disabled before a buyer is selected
tcs.description: Verify that on opening the Create drawer the email, CC and date fields are disabled until a buyer is chosen.
tcs.precond: The Create drawer is freshly opened (no buyer selected).
tcs.steps:
1. Open the Create drawer.
2. Try to interact with Buyer Email, Sales Manager Email, CC and Date fields.
tcs.expected: Buyer Email, Sales Manager Email, CC and Select Date & Time are all disabled until a buyer radio is selected (visual-memory callback-create-drawer.png).

tcs.scenario: To verify Cancel in the Create drawer dismisses without saving
tcs.description: Verify that clicking Cancel closes the Create drawer without creating a request.
tcs.precond: The Create drawer is open (optionally part-filled).
tcs.steps:
1. Optionally select a buyer and pick a date.
2. Click Cancel.
tcs.expected: The drawer closes, no callback request is created, and the table is unchanged.

tcs.scenario: To verify Create submits a request with status REQUESTED + least-loaded assignment
tcs.description: Verify that completing the Create form creates a request in REQUESTED status assigned per the least-loaded rule (self for SM Admin). WRITE action — needs authorisation.
tcs.precond: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a disposable buyer for whom a callback may be created. Requires authorisation (live mutation).
tcs.steps:
1. Open the Create drawer.
2. Search and select the disposable buyer.
3. Pick a Date & Time.
4. Click Create.
5. Find the new row in the table.
tcs.expected: A new callback request is created with status REQUESTED. Assignment follows least-loaded (DOC_DRIFT-CBR-002/004); for an SM Admin creator managerId = self. The new row appears in the table.

tcs.scenario: To verify an isAvailable=false SM is excluded from auto-assignment
tcs.description: Verify that an SM with isAvailable=false is not eligible to receive a newly created callback request. WRITE action — needs authorisation.
tcs.precond: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an SM toggled isAvailable=false + a disposable buyer + the ability to inspect the resulting assignment. Requires authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Ensure a target SM has isAvailable=false.
2. Create a new callback request.
3. Inspect which SM it was assigned to.
tcs.expected: The request is not assigned to the isAvailable=false SM (FS 1.7 #5 / BRD-SM 4.2 isAvailable gate).

tcs.scenario: To verify Create search with no matching buyer shows no results
tcs.description: Verify that a buyer search term matching no customer shows an empty results state in the Create drawer.
tcs.precond: The Create drawer is open.
tcs.steps:
1. Type a non-matching term (e.g. 'ZZZZZNOBUYER999').
2. Click Search.
tcs.expected: The results table shows no rows / an empty state; no buyer can be selected and Create stays disabled. [VERIFY WITH DEV] exact empty-state copy in the Create drawer (FS/BRD silent).

tcs.scenario: To verify the empty state shows when search yields zero rows
tcs.description: Verify that the page renders the 'No data' empty state with a zero total when a search/filter returns no rows.
tcs.precond: The SM is on the Callback Requests page.
tcs.steps:
1. Search for a term that matches nothing.
2. Observe the table area and the total counter.
tcs.expected: The Ant 'No data' empty-state illustration is shown and the counter reads 'Total 0 Callback Requests' (visual-memory callback-empty-state.png).

tcs.scenario: To verify a standard SM sees only their own requests
tcs.description: Verify that a standard Sales Manager (role 5) sees only callback requests assigned to them.
tcs.precond: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a standard SM login with known own + others' requests.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as a standard SM.
2. Review the table rows' Manager column.
tcs.expected: Every row's Manager is the logged-in SM; no other SM's requests appear (FS 1.2 / BRD-SM 4).

tcs.scenario: To verify a non-admin SM sees only own assigned requests
tcs.description: Verify (cross-check of SM_CB_126) that a non-admin SM's table is scoped to their own assigned requests across pages.
tcs.precond: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a standard SM login.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as a standard SM.
2. Page through the table.
3. Verify the Manager column on every page.
tcs.expected: All rows on all pages belong to the logged-in SM; no cross-SM leakage.

tcs.scenario: To verify an SM Admin sees requests across all SMs
tcs.description: Verify that a Sales Manager Admin (role 4) sees callback requests for all SMs system-wide.
tcs.precond: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an SM Admin login with data spanning multiple SMs.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as SM Admin.
2. Review the Manager column across rows.
tcs.expected: Rows for multiple different SMs appear (system-wide view) (FS 1.2 / BRD-SM 4).

tcs.scenario: To verify the Assign action is available only to SM Admin
tcs.description: Verify that the bulk Assign action is present for an SM Admin and absent/disabled for a standard SM.
tcs.precond: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] both an SM Admin and a standard SM login.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as SM Admin; note the Assign button.
2. Log in as standard SM; note whether Assign is present.
tcs.expected: SM Admin sees the 'Assign (N)' bulk button; the standard SM does not (or it is disabled) (BRD-SM 2 — SM Admin reassignment).

tcs.scenario: To verify the SM dropdown filter is available only to SM Admin
tcs.description: Verify that the 'Select Sales Manager' filter dropdown is present for SM Admin and absent for a standard SM.
tcs.precond: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] both an SM Admin and a standard SM login.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as SM Admin; note the Select Sales Manager dropdown.
2. Log in as standard SM; check for the dropdown.
tcs.expected: SM Admin has the 'Select Sales Manager' filter; the standard SM does not (visual-memory callback-filter-open.png is the SM-Admin view).

tcs.scenario: To verify an SM Admin can perform all SM actions plus reassignment
tcs.description: Verify that an SM Admin can capture outcomes and also reassign requests between SMs. WRITE actions — need authorisation.
tcs.precond: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] SM Admin login + disposable requests. Requires authorisation (live mutation).
tcs.steps:
1. As SM Admin, open Capture VC Outcome on a disposable request and confirm it is actionable.
2. Use Assign to reassign a disposable request to another SM.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] SM Admin + disposable requests + target SM
tcs.expected: SM Admin can both capture outcomes and reassign requests; the Manager column reflects the reassignment (BRD-SM 2).

tcs.scenario: To verify SM Admin KPI cards aggregate across all SMs
tcs.description: Verify that for an SM Admin the summary cards aggregate metrics across all SMs.
tcs.precond: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] SM Admin login.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as SM Admin.
2. Read the summary card values.
tcs.expected: The cards reflect system-wide aggregates (consistent with the all-SM table). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm aggregation scope.

tcs.scenario: To verify standard SM KPI cards are scoped to own requests
tcs.description: Verify that for a standard SM the summary cards reflect only that SM's own requests.
tcs.precond: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] standard SM login.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as a standard SM.
2. Read the summary card values.
tcs.expected: The cards reflect only the logged-in SM's own request metrics (scoped).

tcs.scenario: To verify an SM cannot see other SMs' callbacks (managerId scoping) [FSD-CORRECTION]
tcs.description: Verify the managerId-scoping rule that a standard SM cannot retrieve another SM's callback requests even via direct request.
tcs.precond: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] standard SM session + another SM's known request id. API access.
tcs.steps:
1. As a standard SM, request a callback record known to belong to another SM (e.g. by id via the API).
2. Observe the response.
